<SUMMARY>The past week saw significant geopolitical shifts with the United States and Iran reaching a tentative deal to end their conflict, leading to a global rally in stock markets and a drop in oil prices, and President Trump's declaration that the Strait of Hormuz will be completely open by Friday. Concurrently, President Trump announced an ambitious goal to control over 50% of the US chip industry by the end of his term, coinciding with a surge in AI infrastructure development across Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Export controls on advanced AI models, specifically Anthropic's technology, by the US government have sparked discussions on sovereign AI. Critical minerals remain a key focus, with China's rare-earth export value significantly increasing and India actively seeking new supply sources to reduce reliance on China.</SUMMARY>
<EWS>The US federal funding system for scientific research is reportedly crumbling, posing a risk to future innovation. Electric grids in the US are facing strain from the rapid expansion of data center infrastructure, raising concerns about reliability and affordability. Persistent PFAS contamination from a 1992 petrol tanker crash continues to pollute water supplies in Australia's Blue Mountains. The Department of Commerce's restriction of foreign access to Anthropic's most capable AI models, linked to a suspected China-connected Korean telecom, highlights the vulnerability of global access to cutting-edge AI technology. Despite a tentative peace deal, major tanker operators are cautioning against an immediate rush back to the Strait of Hormuz, indicating lingering concerns about security in the region.</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
Taiwan has opened the door for life insurers to invest billions into domestic AI infrastructure, aimed at reducing reliance on foreign assets and enhancing technological growth. The Nikkei Stock Average briefly surpassed the 70,000 mark for the first time on June 16, following the Bank of Japan's decision to raise interest rates. South Korea’s central bank, the Bank of Korea, showed wider support for a hawkish shift in its May meeting minutes, with some policymakers arguing that inflation risks now outweigh the costs of tighter policy. China was struck by a 6.3-magnitude earthquake in Qinghai Province.

**Americas:**
The federal funding system for scientific research in the U.S. is reportedly crumbling. Demand for power from rapidly expanding data center infrastructure is straining electric grids across the U.S., with states and grid operators addressing issues of reliability and affordability. Emerald AI is testing its Conductor software in Virginia for flexible data centers, aiming to ease grid strain.

**Europe:**
IREN has acquired Nostrum, expanding its operations into Europe with an AI cloud platform and adding approximately 490 megawatts of secured power in Spain. The G7 summit in Evian, France, entered its second day with AI and digital security as primary focal points, while crypto was notably absent from discussions. Dozens of malicious wallpapers spreading malware have been found on Steam Workshop, primarily targeting gamers in China and Russia since late 2025.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Asia:**
Taiwan's AI supply chain experienced triple-digit gains in May, driven by surges in server makers and memory chips.

**Americas:**
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) and Amkor Technology have signed a 10-year partnership deal for advanced packaging in Arizona, aiming to accelerate the establishment of a US semiconductor packaging hub. Nokia announced a major expansion of its U.S. semiconductor advanced test and packaging facilities in Pennsylvania to bolster AI growth. The World Direct Write Semiconductor market is undergoing analysis, with forecasts extending to 2035.

**Europe:**
ASML, TSMC, and imec have made a significant advancement in bringing two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor materials from research into high-volume manufacturing, demonstrated at the 2026 IEEE/JSAP Symposium on VLSI Technology and Circuits. Infineon is set to open a fab in Germany as part of a sovereignty push. Intel has commenced production of its anticipated 18A-P chips, driven by continued AI demand. An EU patent allows chips to carry NFTs to verify their origin.
</LITHO>
<REE>
**Asia:**
China's rare-earth export value surged by 44.9% to $243.63 million in Jan-May 2026, despite a modest 2.2% increase in export volumes.

**Africa:**
The EQT Foundation has awarded over €1 Million in grants to researchers from 11 institutions across 9 countries for developing alternatives to critical minerals used in batteries, hydrogen, solar, and industrial systems. The "America’s New Critical Minerals Playbook" from Time Magazine highlights strategic interests in the region. The race for East Africa’s critical minerals is influencing regional conservation efforts, while the DR Congo and Belgium’s colonial-era geological maps are subject to dispute.

**Oceania:**
Sunrise Energy Metals' shares rose by 14.14% due to increasing investor interest in its Syerston scandium project, driven by strategic partnerships and demand for critical minerals in aerospace and clean energy. Western Mines Group has drilled a nickel zone assaying 0.50 per cent nickel from 1303m at its Mulga Tank project in WA, including a 38m section at 0.71 per cent nickel and a single meter at 2.34 per cent. Australian mining billionaire Gina Rinehart's Hancock Prospecting has invested in rare-earth and critical minerals companies, and is exploring potential ties to SpaceX.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
The U.S. has blocked foreign access to Anthropic AI over suspected ties to a China-linked Korean telecom, and the White House was reportedly prepared to issue an export control directive for Claude Mythos.

**Americas:**
Apple previously faced a US export control on its Power Mac G4 in 1999, which Steve Jobs leveraged into a marketing campaign.

**Europe:**
Anthropic's decision to switch off its most capable models worldwide after a US government order to cut foreign access has been cited by Upstage chief Sung Kim as evidence for the necessity of sovereign AI. China issued a ban on German chip giant Infineon.

**Oceania:**
Donald Trump has cut off access to the world’s best AI model, referring to Anthropic's technology.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Americas:**
The FBI and its partners disrupted an alleged explosive-drone plot targeting the UFC Freedom 250 event in Washington, D.C., resulting in five arrests across multiple states. A legal briefing shows that Musk’s Grok AI tool helped guide US strikes on Iran, and the Pentagon later revealed its use in strikes in Iran. SpaceX's Dragon CRS-34 cargo capsule is scheduled to undock and splash down off California, returning bioprinted tissue and cancer-treatment samples from the International Space Station.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>
**Asia:**
Emerging-market stocks are approaching record highs, driven by a tech rally that is shifting capital allocation away from crypto towards equity gains.

**Europe:**
The G7 summit in Evian focused on AI and digital security, suggesting a move towards decentralized regulation for global digital assets.

**Americas:**
President Trump has declared an ambitious goal to achieve over 50% of the U.S. chip industry by the end of his term, a move that could significantly reshape global supply chains and impact US-China relations.
</CONCLUSION>

<INDIA>
Sify Infinit Spaces, an Indian data center operator, has put its ₹3,700 crore IPO on hold, after seeking a valuation of up to $4.2 billion. India's IREL is negotiating with Rosneft to obtain rare earth samples from a Siberian deposit, as part of efforts to reduce reliance on China for these critical minerals. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu is inviting global semiconductor firms to invest in the state, highlighting Andhra Pradesh as a top investment destination and mentioning plans for a semiconductor manufacturing facility. Meta and Reliance are collaborating on AI data centers, and Anthropic has a tie-up with TCS, indicating shifts in India's AI and technology supply chains alongside EV expansion and Starlink delays.
</INDIA>

<WEST_ASIA>
The United States and Iran have reached a tentative deal to end their war, leading to a worldwide rally in stock markets and a drop in oil prices. President Donald Trump has stated that the Strait of Hormuz will be "completely open" by Friday, following months of disruption that impacted global oil markets and prices. Equity markets are facing a long to-do list after the Iran Peace Deal, despite the initial pricing out of a Middle East war. The World Bank cut Myanmar's annual growth forecast to 2% from 3% due to a fuel shock linked to the Middle East conflict. President Trump has called the Iran deal fair and denied US investment in Iran, amid Bitcoin rallying on de-escalation hopes. The world's largest tanker operators are exercising caution regarding an immediate return to the Strait of Hormuz despite the US-Iran deal. Kerun Intelligent Control Co., LTD. has launched Integrated Transformer and Substation Solutions designed for AI data centers in hot-climate regions. A changed Iran is emerging from the war, with implications for its military, leadership, and society after 100 days of conflict and a preliminary peace deal. The New York Times reported on how a deal to end the war in Iran could affect energy prices, while Axios detailed how the Iran war energy crisis defied expectations. Shell's CEO predicts oil prices will continue to rise even after the Iran conflict ends, and ECB officials state that peace in Iran is not enough to fix the energy shock. Foreign Policy analyzed what China might learn from the Iran War. Israel is attempting to catch up in AI, which will likely require millions to change jobs. Musk’s Grok AI tool, used to guide US strikes on Iran, was revealed by a legal briefing and subsequently by the Pentagon.
</WEST_ASIA>

<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
The tentative US-Iran peace deal signals a de-escalation of immediate regional conflict, with a rapid reopening of the Strait of Hormuz poised to stabilize global oil markets. This geopolitical shift, however, occurs amidst a global race for AI dominance, characterized by massive investments in infrastructure, advanced semiconductor manufacturing, and an intensifying focus on critical mineral supply chains. The US administration's aggressive pursuit of domestic chip industry growth and the implementation of export controls on advanced AI models are shaping a bifurcated technological landscape, accelerating the push for sovereign AI capabilities globally. The intersection of geopolitical stability, technological autonomy, and critical resource security will define the strategic environment moving forward.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
